Representative_Docs:
['I just want to start by saying that I have been ordering wigs from Amazon for about 5 years and I have NEVER been more disappointed in a wig in all of this time! The wig that I received is NOTHING like the wig that is advertised! Everything from the cap construction to the length of the hair itself was completely different. The first thing it says in the description is "13X6", but my wig has a 4X6 14" closure. I have very limited parting space and the top is so much shorter than the rest of the wig. I ordered 22 inches, the wig arrived about 18-20 inches and shrank to 16 inches when curled. the ends of the hair are incredibly thin. Another feature listed in the description is "Transparent Lace Pre Plucked". I received ashy beige lace that I then had to tint because it did not blend with my skin the way actual transparent lace does. also the 14 inch 4x6 closure was slightly plucked but rest of the hairline was blunt and untouched. I\'m positive that even if the creator of this wig wanted to pluck the rest of the hairline, they could not because there are tracks location close to the hairline where lace would typically be on an actual 13x6 wig. I had to cut layers in order to blend the short closure in with the rest of the hair. I have no idea where they found the pictures that they use for this wig because it is nothing like what you see pictured. I have never been more disappointed in a human hair wig that I have ordered from Amazon!

I will be updating this review with pictures of everything that I have described.', "Not sure if there are differences in wig standards with these reviews or if we're all reviewing different wigs but the wig I purchased (20 inch, 360 lace, dark brown color, human hair) is not much like the wig that is pictured. I think the only thing they got right was the length. The description on the wig notes that it is indeed the wig I bought but the pictures on Amazon that showcase the wig are false advertising.

In short -- THE BAD:
- LACE: Lace is MUCH darker than what is pictured -- when you put it on, it looks like a hair hat. Not many of us have a scalp that dark.
- PART: There is NO part (middle, side, etc). Are we supposed to do this part ourselves? If so -- make a note of it.
- THICKNESS: The wig is about 6x thicker than what is pictured so it looks fake. It's super heavy and if you put it up in a ponytail, good luck finding a hair tie that can go around it at least once.
- QUALITY: I think it's a mixture of real and synthetic hairs. Upon closer inspection the hair type varies. I did spot quite a few split ends but the thickness of each hair strand isn't consistent which tells me they mixed fibers.
- LACE INTEGRITY: The lace curls up so be prepared to glue it down in case you plan on not returning this wig. I don't think it can be worn glue-less.
- KNOTS: They say they bleached the knots... but they didn't. The front part literally looks like connect the dots on graph paper.
- COLOR: Wig is a mixture of black and dark brown hairs... def. not just dark brown. So, it's much darker than you'd expect it to be per the photos and the description.
- WIG CAP SIZE: I own about 20 wigs. This is the only one that swam on my head (I have a medium sized head). The cap is way too large for me and using the bands will make the outer cap edges curl.
- SCALP CAP: Wearing a cap underneath (black or beige) will show. You can literally see the outline of where it ends on your scalp which is interesting since the lace is so dark.
- CURL: To test if it can curl, I tried it with both a curling iron and natural curlers. Nothing happened (which is further proof to me that they mixed synthetic fibers within the wig).

The Good:
- The baby hairs look decent (although the super visible knots take away from the job they did here).

Maybe if you take it to a salon to get it treated (fade color of lace, bleach the knots, thin the wig out, color correct, high-end band sewing) -- you might make it work. BUT -- how much will that run you up for? I don't think this wig is worth $25... much less the $180 currently advertised. FAKE!

Will upload photos soon.", 'Very thin wig']

Name: 4_hairs_smooth_bad_refund br
Representation: ['hairs', 'smooth', 'bad', 'refund br', 'irritation', 'good shave', 'told', 'shaver', 'foil', 'shaving']
Representative_Docs:
['For two decades I have fought an uphill battle with a downhill class of products, and I\'m throwing in the towel. I\'ve abandoned this electric razor and gone back to a real razor (a basic Gillette Mach 3).

I switched to a multi-headed electric razor over 20 years ago. "Stick with it for 30 days" the instructions implored. Yes, it got better, but never equalled my old 2-blade razor. The convenience suckered me in, and the habit was set. I meticulously cleaned and maintained my electric razors, but never attained a clean shave.

But I stuck with it. Replaced the heads, and that worked for a while, but then same old same old. New electric razors seem to get worse. A little Phillips Philishave 30 worked pretty well (2 heads, *battery* powered), but not great.

When this Arcitec came on board, I said "this is it!" Pricey, but there can be no better, right? Of all the electric razors I have used, I must say that this is the worst. The cleaning system works to a point, but there are inevitably hairs that get lodged in the razor head. And the razor head is effectively *NOT CLEANABLE* except by painstaking surgery to extract lodged hairs.

And the shave? OK, this is not a scientific double-blinded study, but I do honestly believe that this razor provided me with the worst shave of all electric razors I have owned. It got me to jump ship and try a middle-of-the-road Gillette Mach 3. The result ...

HEAVEN! Blades have gotten SO much better since 20 years ago. Super clean shave, no nics, no problems, no irritation ... why did I wait so long??', 'Sent the blades back, as the shave with the new shaver head blades was worse than what I have already on my well used shaver.', "I read with interest, the most favorable review for this shaver. This person mentioned that this is their first electric shaver after a lifetime of using blades. I guess if that is the case, the reviewer doesn't have much to compare this product with. Having had previous Norelco models as well as a Remington and a couple Brauns... I have a bit more actual experience with competing products.

A few years back, we bought a second home. We decided to stock our vacation home with everything needed so that we would not have to carry luggage and we could just head to an airport and go. I had used Norelco shavers for a number of years. About 10 years ago, my wife bought me a Braun 7 series shaver. What a difference. It gave me a much smoother and closer shave with less chafing and discomfort. I wasn't and still am not impressed with the so-called cleaning system that Bruan has designed. But the shaver itself was terrific. About 2 years ago, the battery in my beloved Braun started to fail. So I bought a new 790CC Braun Shaver. This one was even better than the first. So as we gathered things to take to our second home, I asked my wife to pick up another Braun shaver. The 790CC is not an inexpensive product. So my thrifty wife, knowing I had used Norelcos in the past, picked up the Arcitec shaver on sale.

What a disappointment! To be honest, I can't find anything that is a distinct positive about this product. Let me organize my thoughts just a bit...

1. Size - The shaver head is just too big. It is hard to maneuver in tight areas such as at the upper lip and nose. Requires using the trimmer to get acceptably close.
2. Performance - I do not have a heavy beard. I find that 24 hours of growth is the limit for this shaver. If your facial hair is allowed to grow for any longer than that, the shaver will not cut it. If you have a heavy beard, this shaver simply wont do the job.
3. Cleaning - The heads clog very quickly. Once they do, the shaver will not cut at all. The Braun by comparison, can usually go a week before cleaning.
4. Trimmer - As others have said... Small and in an awkward position. It's foolish to suggest that the shaver head should be removed to facilitate trimming. Better to suggest that the Phillips/Norelco engineers should take a crack at a better design.

I have used this shaver intermittently for the last two years. My older Norelcos were far better than this one. So that being said, I finally decided enough is enough and ordered another Braun from Amazon."]

Returning.", "AWFUL. I was really hoping this mascara would fill the sad, gaping hole left by the discontinuance of Scandal Queen, which was the most perfect, amazing mascara EVER, but nope, the Quattro Film Type mascara is a hugely over-priced disaster.

Representative_Docs:
["I bought these for my son for Christmas because the description claims they are organic and 100% natural. I was looking for bath bombs with no artificial dyes. I even asked if the bombs had artificial dyes and someone responded they did not. That is not accurate. The ingredients on the box include artificial dyes yet the box says 100% organic. I don't understand how something could claim to be 100% organic and natural with artificial coloring. I feel misled.", 'There has been much discussion about this product on Amazon and professional nail tech blogs. One of the most serious issues is the absence of a safety data sheet (SDS) from the manufacturer. By law, manufacturers selling chemical products in the United States must provide accurately documented SDS upon request. The manufacturer of this product has not provided such a SDS. We ordered a product through Amazon which arrived via China Post/USPS identified as \'Makeup Tools\' for customs purposes. As professional chemists, we analyzed this product (pH, FTIR, TGA, elemental analysis and GC-MS). This alkaline product contains methylene chloride, methanol, n-butoxyethanol, a series of n-alkane hydrocarbons and two different petroleum boiling point distillate fractions. Methylene chloride and methanol are known toxic chemicals which can be absorbed through the skin and inhaled into your respiratory tract. Please use Google to search for and open the SDS docs for these two chemicals and read the hazards. This product is similar to a methylene chloride containing industrial paint strippers which are being removed from the marketplace due to their toxic ingredient(s). This product is not suitable for sale to the general public or to the professional nail community as a nail polish remover. AMAZON is derelict in its duty to police the products it sells; in this case the product is highlighted as "Amazon\'s Choice". Please be aware that there are other brands of \'Magic Remover\' being offered for sale with a similar name, paper label and bottle shape. Buyer Beware!', 'This claims to be titanium dioxide free, gluten free, made with natural and organic ingredients, vegan, and free of parabens, nano-particles, bismuth oxychloride, talc, silicones, mineral oil, GMOs, artificial fragrance, artificial preservatives, FD&C dyes, carmine, and phthalates. It is made in the USA. The ingredient list is on the product box and it is really short (see photos). It claims to be formulated with natural ingredients, such as\xa0Kaolin Clay\xa0and Jojoba Oil. They say they are cruelty free. The product page has a photo that says “Leaping Bunny Certified,” but the logo on the box is a PETA logo. I checked both websites and HYNT Beauty is certified by both Leaping Bunny and PETA.

I got the shade “Linen Kiss.” A little searching online showed it was a matte ivory. I really didn’t like they didn’t have much info at all about the shades to choose from. There weren’t any descriptions of the different shades to say whether they were matte, shimmer, etc. There weren’t photos other than the product in the little singles compact. I would have liked to have seen more product photos, like swatches comparing the different shades to help me choose, or at least a description of each shade. I had to search on Google and even when I went to their website there were only 4 shade options there. At least there they had a description for the 4 shades, but they only had the single photo of each in the singles compact. For a single eyeshadow coating $22, I expect more. The focus on the ingredients and what isn’t included is good, but they should also put a little attention on providing customers with more photos so they can easily pick a shade that’s right for them and be happy when the get it. Not have to guess what finish it has or if they shade is going to look like it does in the pan when they get it.

This comes in a little ziplock bag. Inside is a little outer product box.

It comes in a plastic singles compact. The top flips open easily.

It’s a matte ivory.

I show a photo where I swatched it. I did a finger swatch on my clean forearm (no lotion, primer, etc.). I swirled my finger in the pan and it seemed really hard pressed, like I wasn’t picking up much. I looked at my finger to see what I had picked up and should have been surprised after how much I swirled it in the pan that I didn’t have more, but I wasn’t really because of how hard pressed it felt. I took a photo showing it on my finger. As you can see, it isn’t very opaque and doesn’t look like I picked much up. I swirled a lot and that’s all I got. I swiped that onto my forearm. Then I went back into the pan. This time I pressed harder into the pan while I swirled. I picked up the same amount and put a second layer over the first one I had already done. Then, I did the same thing and did a different swipe. I did 3 layers for that one to show how it built up. It showed up enough on my fair skin, but I wasn’t a fan with how hard pressed this was. Maybe if I didn’t get such a light shade I’d like it more? But, I feel like the formula just isn’t too great and wouldn’t have great pigmentation with any color.

It’s nice and smooth.

Overall, its okay. It’s not for me. For me to spend $22 for a single eyeshadow, the eyeshadow needs to be pretty darn good. This just isn’t it. It’s too hard pressed for my liking. You don’t pick up much product and even when you do it doesn’t have that much pigmentation. Like I said, maybe with a different color it would be different, but I don’t think so. There’s way better options out there. I don’t recommend this.']
